name: tmux
summary: A terminal multiplexer that keeps a server-owned session graph of clients, sessions, windows, and panes, connects panes to PTYs, and routes parsed commands and terminal events across persistent server and client processes.

features.name: Server and client process boundary
features.description: tmux separates a long-lived server from client processes; clients connect to the server to attach, display, and issue commands while the server owns session state and pane processes.
benefits: Sessions can outlive an attaching terminal client
Control and presentation are separate process roles
costs: Socket connection and server lifecycle add failure modes
State ownership across processes requires synchronization

features.name: Session, window, and pane topology
features.description: The server composes sessions from windows and panes, supports current and grouped client views, and applies commands that create, select, split, move, resize, or destroy topology nodes.
benefits: Provides persistent named workspaces with multiple terminal panes
Makes layout and attachment state explicit
costs: Topology changes must coordinate focus, size, and process lifetime
Multiple clients can observe or mutate shared state

features.name: PTY and terminal I/O loop
features.description: Panes own PTY-backed processes and terminal state; the server reads and writes pane streams, updates screen state, and sends terminal output to attached clients through tty handling.
benefits: Preserves interactive shell behavior behind a persistent session
Centralizes pane output for multiple clients
costs: PTY and terminal semantics remain host-specific
High output rates compete with client redraw and input handling

features.name: Command parser and control dispatch
features.description: tmux parses command lines and key-driven command sequences into command objects, queues them for execution, and exposes operations for sessions, windows, panes, options, buffers, and clients.
benefits: Offers one control vocabulary for interactive and scripted operations
Supports ordered command queues and conditional control
costs: Command parsing and quoting are a compatibility surface
Control authority reaches shared session resources

mathematical_views.question: How do a server, clients, sessions, windows, panes, and child processes attach and detach?
assumptions: The server is the authoritative topology owner
Attachment does not prove child-process persistence after server teardown

mathematical_views.question: How does pane process output become terminal state and client-visible redraw data?
assumptions: The server maintains pane terminal state
TTY presentation and client scheduling are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which client or command can mutate a session, window, pane, option, or buffer?
assumptions: Server access policy selects reachable resources
The model does not prove socket deployment security
